t.7.38.1: Those great-souled kings, the heroes, departed joyfully in every direction for their own cities, making the earth tremble as they went.
t.7.38.2: They had assembled in many thousands of akṣauhiṇīs, all gathered together for the sake of Rāghava; now they all departed, joyful.
t.7.38.3: And the kings, filled with strength and pride, said: “Indeed, we do not see Rāvaṇa standing before us in battle.”
t.7.38.5: Protected by the might of the arms of Rāma and of Lakṣmaṇa, we could fight with ease on the far shore of the ocean, free from fever and fear.
t.7.38.4: We were brought here afterwards by Bharata to no purpose, for the rākṣasas there would have been slain by the kings; of this there is no doubt.
t.7.38.6: Telling these and other tales there by the thousands, those kings, mighty chariot-warriors, entered their own kingdoms.
t.7.38.7: Having gone back each to his own city, those kings gave Rāma gifts and jewels of many kinds, wishing to do what would please him.
t.7.38.8: Horses, jewels and garments, and elephants fierce with the frenzy of rut, heavenly sandal-pastes and heavenly ornaments as well.
t.7.38.9: Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, and the great chariot-warrior Śatrughna took those jewels and went back again to Ayodhyā.
t.7.38.10: And those bulls among men, having arrived at the delightful city of Ayodhyā, gave all their jewels to the great-souled Rāghava.
t.7.38.11: Having accepted all that, Rāghava, filled with delight, gave all those things to the great-souled Sugrīva.
t.7.38.13: Then all those mighty ones, their hearts delighted, bore upon their heads and upon their arms those gifts that Rāma had given them.
t.7.38.12: He gave also to Vibhīṣaṇa, and to those others who were there: the bears and monkeys, heroes led by Hanumān, and the mighty rākṣasas.
t.7.38.14: They drank fragrant meads of many kinds, and they savoured well-prepared meats and fruits.
t.7.38.15: Thus, while they dwelt there, a month and more then passed; out of their devotion to Rāma, they deemed all that time to be but a single moment.
t.7.38.16: That Rāma took delight in the company of those monkeys, who could change their form at will, and of the kings of great valor, and of the rākṣasas of great strength.
t.7.38.17: Thus for them, the delighted monkeys and the rākṣasas all together, the second month, a month of the cool season, passed happily.
